answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new agent to earn entry through a trellis of peer endorsements: established agents stake a small bond to vouch for a newcomer, and the bond is slashed if the newcomer spams or double-spends. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but crossing the canyon of trust at scale means buying endorsements from many independent, reputable agents, each costing real stake and exposing the endorser. A single pearl of genuine work history is therefore worth more than a thousand empty shells, because reputation accrues slowly and cannot be cloned.
